Below is a complete, consolidated 12‑week programme (start 2026‑06‑01) for your 47‑year‑old advanced female client in early perimenopause with significant vasomotor symptoms and heat intolerance. It integrates: periodised resistance training (primary), bone‑health emphasis, nutrition to support perimenopause and bone density, cardio to maintain aerobic fitness, mobility alternatives to hot yoga, cooling/vasomotor management, and testing guidance (including conditions for 1RM testing at the end of the cycle). Phase 2 intensity has been pushed per your request. Hot yoga and fasted morning HIIT have been excluded for safety; safe alternatives are included.

High‑level overview
- Duration: 12 weeks, start 2026‑06‑01
- Training frequency: 4 resistance sessions/week (Upper/Lower split + power/hybrid days), 2 cardio sessions/week (plus 1 optional recovery session), 2 mobility sessions/week (cool yoga / pool or restorative).
- Phases:
  - Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation & symptom‑adjusted conditioning (re‑establish technique, moderate volume, cooling routine).
  - Phase 2 (Weeks 4–8): Intensification & strength push (higher intensity — planned singles/doubles/doubles and heavy 3–5RM ranges, reduced accessory volume on heavy weeks).
  - Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Peak/variation & consolidation (maintain gains, taper Week 12; Week 12 testing option if readiness criteria met).
- Testing: 3RM testing during Week 7 (optional) and conditional 1RM testing at end of Week 12 if readiness checklist satisfied.
- Cooling protocol: pre‑cool (10–15 min cold shower/ice towels), in‑session cooling (fan, mist bottle, cold drinks, neck towel), post‑session cold shower + rehydration. Schedule sessions in cooler parts of day and avoid saunas/hot tubs.
- Nutrition: daily targets (protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg BW, calcium 1000–1200 mg/day, vitamin D supplementation as needed, adequate carbs around heavy sessions, hydration/electrolytes). Mild calorie surplus for strength gains (+150–250 kcal) unless fat loss desired — then small deficit only with caution.
- Cardio: 2 structured sessions/week — Cardio A (steady aerobic base 30–50 min) and Cardio B (short intervals/tempo in cool environment or pool). Avoid fasted HIIT; recommend fed HIIT or pool intervals if higher intensity desired.
- Mobility: replace hot yoga with room‑temperature yoga, pool yoga, yin/restorative yoga, Pilates, and two coached mobility sessions/week. Include breathing/mindfulness to mitigate vasomotor triggers.
- Autoregulation: monitor RPE, sleep, hot flash frequency/severity, readiness; reduce volume if symptoms or sleep decline.

Week‑by‑week plan (detailed)

Phase 1 — Foundation & Symptom‑Adjusted Conditioning (Weeks 1–3)
General guidance
- Main lifts: moderate intensity, technique focus. RPE ~7–8 on main sets, leave 1–2 RIR Week 1 → 0–1 RIR by Week 3 for main lifts.
- Accessory sets: 3–4 sets, 8–12 reps mostly.
- Cardio: conservative; pool or bike preferred.
- Mobility: 2 sessions/week (45–60 min room‑temp yoga or pool yoga / restorative).

Week 1 (2026‑06‑01 to 2026‑06‑07)
- Day 1 (Mon) — Lower heavy
  - Back squat 4 × 5 @ ~75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift 3 × 6–8
  - Walking Bulgarian split squat 3 × 8/leg
  - Glute bridge 3 × 10
  - Pallof press 3 × 10/side
- Day 2 (Tue) — Upper heavy
  - Bench press 4 × 5 @ ~75% 1RM
  - Bent‑over/chest‑supported row 4 × 6
  - Overhead press 3 × 6
  - Pull‑ups/lat pulldown 3 × 6–8
  - Face pulls 3 × 12
- Day 3 (Wed) — Cardio A: 30 min bike or pool (easy); Mobility session (45 min room‑temp yoga)
- Day 4 (Thu) — Lower hybrid
  - Trap bar deadlift 4 × 4 (moderate)
  - Front squat 3 × 6
  - Step‑ups 3 × 8/leg
  - Hamstring curl 3 × 12
  - Calf raises 3 × 12–15
- Day 5 (Fri) — Upper hypertrophy + Cardio B (optional short)
  - Incline DB press 4 × 8
  - Single‑arm row 3 × 10/side
  - Lateral raises + band pull‑aparts 3 × 12/12
  - Biceps curl 3 × 10
  - Hanging knee raises 3 × 10
  - Optional Cardio B: 8 × 30 s hard / 90 s easy on bike if cool/later in day
- Day 6–7 (Sat–Sun) — Rest / light walk / mobility

Week 2
- Progress main lift loads by ~2–4% or add 1–2 reps; maintain cooling strategy. Cardio A: 30–35 min, cardio B: short intervals or skip if heat.

Week 3
- Main lifts: 4 × 4 @ 78–80% 1RM for squat/bench. Reintroduce 1 short metabolic finisher (only if cool environment). Mobility twice weekly.

Phase 2 — Intensification & Strength Push (Weeks 4–8)
Key adjustments
- Increase intensity: main lifts move to 3–5RM ranges and include planned singles/doubles in Weeks 5 & 7.
- Reduce accessory volume on peak heavy weeks (Weeks 5 & 7) by ~15–25%.
- Keep cardio but reduce volume on heavy weeks; use pool/bike and schedule away from heavy lifts by 6–12 hours.
- Maintain bone‑focused nutrition: ↑carbs on heavy days, protein constant.

Week 4 (start heavier)
- Day 1 — Lower heavy
  - Back squat 6 × 4 @ ~83–86% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift 4 × 5
  - Bulgarian split squat 3 × 6–8
  - Heavy glute bridge 3 × 6–8
  - Core 3 × 8
- Day 2 — Upper heavy
  - Bench press 6 × 4 @ ~83–86% 1RM
  - Bent‑over row 5 × 5
  - Overhead press 4 × 5
  - Weighted pull‑ups 4 × 5–6
- Day 3 — Cardio A 35 min bike/pool (easy), Mobility (45 min)
- Day 4 — Lower power/hybrid
  - Deadlift doubles 5 × 2 @ 85–88% (or 4 × 3 @ 82–85%)
  - Front squat 4 × 4
  - Good mornings/RDL 3 × 6
  - Calves 3 × 10–12
- Day 5 — Upper strength accessories 4 × 6 heavy; short cardio if tolerated

Week 5 (heavy intensity week)
- Day 1 — Lower max doubles/singles
  - Back squat work to 3–4 singles or 3 doubles at 90–93% (limit attempts)
  - RDL 3 × 5
  - Heavy step‑ups 3 × 6/leg
  - Farmer carries 3 × 40–60 m
- Day 2 — Upper heavy singles/doubles
  - Bench to heavy doubles/single at ~90–92%
  - Heavy rows 4 × 4
  - Overhead press 3 × 4
- Day 3 — Cardio: 20–30 min easy pool or complete rest
- Day 4 — Lower moderate (4 × 3 deadlifts @ 85–88%)
- Day 5 — Upper hypertrophy light sets (3–4 × 8–10)
- Recovery priority: sleep, hydration, cooling between heavy attempts. Reduce cardio volume.

Week 6 (sustain high intensity)
- Day 1 — Back squat 5 × 3 @ 86–88%
- Day 2 — Bench 5 × 3 @ 86–88%
- Day 4 — Speed deadlifts 8 × 2 @ 55–65% (with bands/chains if available)
- Day 5 — Upper hybrid heavy accessories
- Cardio: Cardio A 35–40 min; Cardio B intervals short (8 × 45 s/75 s) in cool place.

Week 7 (test/peak week)
- Day 1 — Lower test (3RM or heavy doubles; monitor signs)
  - Warm up rigorously and follow cooling cycle
  - Limit attempts; stop if hot flashes escalate
- Day 2 — Upper test (3RM or heavy doubles)
- Day 3 — Recovery pool session + mobility
- Day 4 — Light speed/technique; Day 5 — short accessory maintenance
- Cardio: low intensity/pool only this week; reduce interval work.

Week 8 (controlled deload while retaining intensity)
- Day 1 — Back squat 4 × 2–3 @ 88–90% (fewer sets)
- Day 2 — Bench 4 × 2–3 @ 88–90%
- Day 4 — Speed work lighter; Day 5 — upper moderate 3–4 × 8
- Cardio: 1–2 low intensity sessions; mobility twice.

Phase 3 — Peak/Variation & Consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
Goals
- Consolidate strength/hypertrophy, maintain aerobic fitness, recovery optimization, and prepare for conditional 1RM testing at Week 12 if readiness met.
- Taper volume in Week 12; maintain some high intensity but reduce total volume.

Week 9
- Reintroduce mixed rep ranges:
  - Lower: back squat 6 × 3 @ ~85% (or doubles)
  - Deadlift heavy 4 × 5
  - Upper: paused benching, close‑grip bench 3–4 × 5–6
- Cardio: Cardio A 40 min; Cardio B intervals or tempo in pool/cool environment.
- Mobility: 2 sessions/week.

Week 10
- Mixed rep focus and quality:
  - Lower: heavy triples/doubles with moderate accessory volume
  - Upper: 6–8 rep work for hypertrophy on assistance; maintain heavy single/double for neural retention
- Cardio: Cardio A 40–45 min; Cardio B tempo 15–20 min in cool area or pool intervals.
- Nutrition: maintain carbs on heavy days.

Week 11
- Tapering starts — reduce volume by ~15–20% while keeping intensity in selected lifts; one longer low‑intensity cardio session (50–60 min) if tolerated.
- Mobility and breathing focus: include restorative yoga or pool yoga sessions; stress reduction.

Week 12 (Deload & Conditional 1RM testing)
- Goal: Deload overall volume ~30% and prepare for 1RM testing if readiness checklist is met; otherwise do submaximal 3–5RM tests and estimate 1RMs.
- Testing protocol (conditional):
  - Check readiness checklist (sleep ≥7 h average, stable vasomotor symptoms past 2 weeks, good recovery, well‑fuelled and hydrated).
  - Schedule testing in cool, climate‑controlled gym; limit number of maximal attempts per lift to 3–5; allow 3–5 min rest and active cooling between attempts.
  - Recommended order (if testing all): squat → bench → deadlift → overhead press OR split across two days with 24–48 h between heavy tests.
  - If any adverse symptoms occur, abort and revert to 3RM test.
- If not testing: perform lighter technique sessions, maintain mobility and recovery, and record best heavy set numbers for progress.

Detailed weekly session templates (typical week example — mid‑cycle heavy week)
- Mon — Lower heavy
  - Warm‑up + cooling protocol
  - Main: Back squat 5 × 3 @ 86–88%
  - RDL 4 × 5
  - Split squats 3 × 6–8
  - Glute bridges 3 × 6–8
  - Core: planks 3 × 45 s
- Tue — Upper heavy
  - Bench press 5 × 3 @ 86–88%
  - Pendlay/bent‑over row 4 × 5
  - OHP 4 × 5
  - Pull‑ups weighted 4 × 5
  - Face pulls 3 × 12
- Wed — Cardio A 35–40 min bike/pool + mobility (45 min yoga)
- Thu — Lower power/hybrid
  - Speed deadlifts 8 × 2 @ 55–65%
  - Front squat 4 × 4
  - Hamstring curl 3 × 10
  - Calves 3 × 12
- Fri — Upper hypertrophy + Cardio B intervals
  - Incline DB press 4 × 6–8 heavy
  - Chest‑supported row 4 × 6
  - Lat/shoulder accessory 3 × 8–12
  - Cardio B: 8 × 45 s/75 s on bike (cool)
- Sat — Mobility (pool yoga or restorative) or optional low intensity walk
- Sun — Rest

Cardio plan (summary)
- Cardio A: steady aerobic base, 30→50 min progressive across phases (pool/bike preferred).
- Cardio B: short intervals or tempo in cool environment or pool. Progress intervals from short work (30 s) to 45–60 s with reduced rest as tolerated.
- Reduce cardio volume on heavy weeks (Weeks 5 & 7); favor pool sessions for higher intensity with low thermal stress.
- Avoid fasted HIIT. If she wants HIIT, it must be fed and in a cool environment or pool.

Nutrition plan summary (perimenopause + bone health)
- Calories: Maintenance +150–250 kcal for lean mass gain (or small 200–300 kcal deficit only if fat loss is priority and symptoms tolerable).
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg BW/day, evenly split across 3–4 meals (20–40 g per meal).
- Carbohydrate: 2.5–4 g/kg/day based on training load — concentrate carbs around heavy sessions (pre/post).
- Fat: 0.8–1.2 g/kg/day, emphasise unsaturated fats and omega‑3s.
- Calcium: 1000–1200 mg/day from diet ± supplements; split doses 300–500 mg per meal for absorption.
- Vitamin D: 1000–2000 IU/day or as advised by GP after blood test.
- Magnesium: 300–400 mg/day via food/supplement at night if sleep/cramps present (check with GP).
- Omega‑3: 1–2 g EPA+DHA/day if diet low in oily fish.
- Avoid/limit triggers: caffeine, alcohol, spicy foods before training or bedtime if they provoke hot flashes.
- Hydration & electrolytes: sip fluids before/during/after sessions; electrolyte drink on heavy sweat days.
- Supplements to discuss with GP: vitamin D, calcium supplement if dietary shortfall, magnesium, omega‑3, collagen (optional), multivitamin.

Mobility and flexibility (hot‑safe alternatives)
- Replace hot yoga with:
  - Room‑temperature vinyasa or restorative yoga twice weekly (45–60 min), or
  - Pool yoga / aqua yoga 30–45 min twice weekly, or
  - Yin/restorative yoga + Pilates mix if preferred.
- Daily 10–15 min mobility routine (thoracic rotation, hip flexor stretches, hamstring holds 2–3 min) after easy cardio or on rest days.
- Incorporate diaphragmatic breathing and paced exhalations to mitigate sympathetic activation and reduce hot flash triggers.

Cooling & vasomotor management (to use every session)
- Pre‑cool: 10–15 min cold shower or neck/wrist ice towels.
- In‑session: fan directed at client, mist bottle, cold towel on back of neck, cold beverage sips, longer rests between heavy sets (3–5 min when pushing singles/doubles).
- Post‑session: cool shower, chilled clothing, electrolyte rehydration.
- Schedule heavy sessions early morning in cool gym or late afternoon when ambient temps are lower. Avoid heat exposures (sauna/hot tubs) entirely.

Cardio & HIIT safety

Phase 3 — Peak/Variation & Consolidation (Weeks 9–12)
Goals
- Consolidate strength/hypertrophy, maintain aerobic fitness, recovery optimization, and prepare for conditional 1RM testing at Week 12 if readiness met.

  - Schedule testing in cool, climate‑controlled gym; limit number of maximal attempts per lift to 3–5; allow 3–5 min rest and active cooling between attempts.
  - Recommended order (if testing all): squat → bench → deadlift → overhead press OR split across two days with 24–48 h between heavy tests.
  - If any adverse symptoms occur, abort and revert to 3RM test.
